newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to prop up domestic sugar prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to prop up domestic sugar prices.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos has ordered the National Food Authority (NFA) to intervene in the sugar market to prop up falling prices, the presidential palace said on Wednesday.

Ramos has signed an executive order authorising the NFA to procure raw sugar from farmers "in such volume as it may deem necessary in consultation with the Department of Agriculture," the palace said.
The order did not give any procurement prices.
The order said there was "an urgent need to stabilise the price of sugar .. brought about by the low farmgate prices thereof to the detriment of farmer-producers".
Traders have said over-importation of sugar has led to a glut and falling prices.
Farmers have said costs of raw sugar production are 627 pesos per 50-kg bag while current farmgate prices are only 530 pesos.
The government's Sugar Regulatory Administration has however estimated production costs at only 488 pesos per 50-kg bag.
